newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba-July M3 growth down as private lending slowed.
newsitem.headline: Buba-July M3 growth down as private lending slowed.

text.p: German M3 money supply growth slowed to an annualised rate of 5.7 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June as lending to the private sector slowed and money capital formation picked up, the Bundesbank said Tuesday.
Growth also slowed because domestic non-banks resumed buying money market fund certificates for the first time since February 1996.
Buba-July M3 growth down as private lending slowed

"The M3 money supply in July...again grew moderately," the Bundesbank said in a statement. "A slowdown in lending to the private sector and stronger money capital formation acted as brakes on the expansion of the money supply."
But the Bundesbank added that public sector demand for credit and net fund inflows from domestic non-banks' foreign transactions continued to have an "expansive" effect on the money supply.

The July figure puts M3 inside the Bundesbank's 1997 target growth corridor of 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent for the second month running. The growth rate is below economists' forecast which had averaged 6.3 percent.

The Bundesbank said sight deposits expanded exceptionally strongly in July after falling in June. Savings deposits with statutory three-month notice period also grew strongly while the amount of cash in circulation virtually stagnated.
Domestic non-banks increased their holdings of money market fund certificates by a net 0.7 billion marks in July, the first monthly net increase since February 1996, the Bundesbank said.
Expanded M3, an indicator introduced by the Bundesbank to include the impact of money market funds, grew moderately in June, the last month for which such data are available.
Meanwhile money capital formation at banks accelerated in July, with annualised growth over the last six months through July accelerating to 5.5 percent from 4.3 percent in June.
